test_title: SSC Stenographer 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 08 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Choose the correct active voice form of the sentence:

"All the books had been neatly arranged on the shelves by my grandfather."

options.text: My grand father has neatly arranged all the books on the shelves.
My grand father had arranged all the books on the shelves.
My grand father have neatly arranged all the books on the shelves.
My grand father had neatly arranged all the books on the shelves.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence is in passive voice: "All the books had been neatly arranged on the shelves by my grandfather."
 
• To convert to active voice, the subject "my grandfather" should perform the action.
 
• The correct active voice structure is: "My grandfather had neatly arranged all the books on the shelves."
 
• The verb "had been arranged" in passive voice becomes "had neatly arranged" in active voice.
 
• The sentence retains the past perfect tense.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"My grandfather had neatly arranged all the books on the shelves."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: **"My grandfather has neatly arranged all the books on the shelves." – Incorrect tense (present perfect).
 
• **Option 2: **"My grandfather had arranged all the books on the shelves." – Missing "neatly," which is part of the original sentence.
 
• **Option 3: **"My grandfather have neatly arranged all the books on the shelves." – Incorrect subject-verb agreement ("have" should be "had").
